test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jul 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They are the people __which are looking to expand__ their horizons in the fast growing tourism industry.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e.** 'who are looking to expand'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sentence is referring** to the group of people who have a certain aim to expand their horizons in the tourism industry. In English grammar, when** referring to** **people**, we use** 'who'** not '**which'.**
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the usage of the relative pronoun 'which' for referring to people. The correct relative pronoun to use for people is 'who'.
 
• The verb form **'are looking to expand'** correctly maintains agreement with the plural subject (the people).

Therefore, the** corrected sentence** should be "*They are the people **who are looking to expand** their horizons in the fast growing tourism industry."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **'which looked to expand' is incorrect because 'which' is not the correct relative pronoun to refer to people. Also, the use of past tense 'looked' is not consistent with the other verbs of the sentence that are in the present tense.
 
• **Option 2: **'who is looking to expand' is grammatically incorrect. 'Is looking' would be incorrect verb agreement for the plural subject 'people'.
 
• **Option 4:** 'that are looked to expand' is grammatically incorrect. The verb phrase 'are looked to expand' doesn't make sense in the context of the sentence.
